# Zellij

**Role:** terminal multiplexer inside Ghostty — panes, tabs, detachable/resurrectable sessions.
Deliberately near-invisible: it starts locked so the shell and Neovim keep almost every keystroke.

**Config:** `home/dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` (autogenerated by zellij's config UI, then hand-patched);
`default_layout "compact"` is built-in; plugin binary from `home/.chezmoiexternal.toml`. zellij **0.44.3**.

## Locked-by-default design

- `default_mode "locked"` + `keybinds clear-defaults=true`, so the whole keymap is spelled out in the
  repo file: 176 bindings, one key each.
- Audited line-by-line against `zellij setup --dump-config` for 0.44.3: **101 bindings are stock
  defaults replayed verbatim** (`origin: default`), **67 are genuine deviations** (`custom`), **8 are
  the navigator plugin** (`plugin`). No stock default is missing, and nothing in the file is
  unaccounted for in `zellij.json`.
- The dominant deviation is the *return target*: 57 bindings swap stock's `SwitchToMode "normal"` for
  `SwitchToMode "locked"`, so mode-exit chords, one-shot actions and `Esc`/`Enter` land back in locked.
  This is **not** derived from `default_mode` — tested with stock keybinds and `--default-mode locked`,
  leaving pane mode puts you in *normal* (`Ctrl+Q` still quits). It is this config's own behaviour.
- Only 6 bindings have no stock counterpart at all: locked `Alt+N`, the four locked `Alt+arrow`
  navigator bindings, and `F1` → compact-bar `toggle_tooltip` (paired with `tooltip "F1"` on the alias).
- In locked mode exactly 7 keys do anything: `Ctrl+G` (unlock — the only stock locked binding),
  `Alt+N`, the four `Alt+arrow` navigator bindings, `F1` via the `shared` block.
- Mode-entry chords are stock (`Ctrl+P/T/N/H/S/O/B`); only their exits deviate. `normal` has no block
  of its own — purely transient, reachable only via `Ctrl+G`.

## Navigator plugin

`Alt+←↓↑→` are `MessagePlugin` calls into `vim-zellij-navigator.wasm` (hiasr **0.3.0**, pinned in
`home/.chezmoiexternal.toml`). Verified against the 0.3.0 README: `move_focus` / `move_focus_or_tab`
are real commands, left/right use `move_focus_or_tab` (wraps to prev/next tab at the edge), up/down use
`move_focus`, and `move_mod` / `use_arrow_keys` are real config keys — which the README requires on
*every* binding, as done here (`locked` plus `shared_except "locked" "scroll"`). Caveat: the README only
documents `shared_except "locked"`; the extra copy inside `locked` is a local extension. Unverifiable
here: whether nvim consumes the forwarded Alt+arrows — `~/.config/nvim` is not chezmoi-managed.

## Quirks

- **macOS:** Alt = Option; needs `macos-option-as-alt = true` + `option+left/right=unbind` in
  `home/dot_config/ghostty/config` (lines 5, 11-12) so real Alt+arrow CSI reaches zellij.
- **Scroll mode is a navigator dead zone** (lines 127-135): raw `MoveFocus`/`MoveFocusOrTab`, no nvim
  forwarding, and unlike stock's Alt nav it appends `SwitchToMode "locked"`. `Alt+hjkl` (254-257)
  bypasses the plugin too — only the arrow variants are nvim-aware.
- `SwitchFocus` (pane `p`) is absent from zellij's documented action list — "next pane" is inferred and
  flagged unverified in the JSON.
- Theme still `catppuccin-macchiato`, not gruvbox-material (TODO); `pane_frames false`; tmux-compat mode
  (`Ctrl+B`, 19 bindings, 15 deviating only by return-to-locked) is populated though tmux is gone.
